name: Loch Leglean Tribunal
description: The Hermetic tribunal covering Scotland north of Hadrian's Wall, named for Pralix's winter camp; the largest tribunal by number of magi, dominated by House Ex Miscellanea.

name: Hibernian Tribunal
description: Hermetic tribunal covering Ireland, created when the British Isles were divided into three tribunals in 817.

name: Stonehenge Tribunal
description: Hermetic tribunal covering Britain up to Hadrian's Wall, neighbor of Loch Leglean.

name: Normandy Tribunal
description: Hermetic tribunal growing in importance to Loch Leglean because of mundane ties between Scotland and France.

name: Order of Hermes
description: The order of Hermetic magi, founded at Durenmar in 767; in Scotland it has a checkered past and many unorthodox practices.

name: House Ex Miscellanea
description: The thirteenth House, formed from Pralix's Ordo Miscellanea in 817; comprises half the magi of the Loch Leglean Tribunal.

name: Ordo Miscellanea
description: Order of non-Hermetic magicians founded by Pralix after the war against Damhan-allaidh in opposition to the Order of Hermes; later admitted as House Ex Miscellanea.

name: House Mercere
description: Hermetic House of messengers (Redcaps); has only one member in the Loch Leglean Tribunal.

name: House Quaesitor
description: Hermetic House of investigators and judges; its only member in Loch Leglean is Whitburh Frithowebba of Horsingas.

name: House Flambeau
description: Hermetic House of combat magi; fought Damhan-allaidh, rampaged through the Highlands in 1099, and has bad blood with House Ex Miscellanea; fewer than five members in Scotland.

name: House Tremere
description: Hermetic House whose followers opposed Damhan-allaidh and helped destroy House Diedne in the Schism War.

name: House Tytalus
description: Hermetic House of Pralix; its magi fought Damhan-allaidh in 814 and again in 889.

name: House Diedne
description: Druidic Hermetic House that aided Kenneth MacAlpin against the Picts and eradicated the Pictish tongue; destroyed in the Schism War.

name: House Merinita
description: Hermetic House of faerie magic; the second largest House in Loch Leglean with ten magi.

name: House Bonisagus
description: Hermetic House of Trianoma.

name: House Guernicus
description: Name used for the Quaesitorial House in a Flambeau letter asking for a tribunal to judge Horsingas.

name: Order of Odin
description: Supposed order of Scandinavian wizards feared by Hermetic magi; in truth Norse magicians have no formal order, and quaesitores treat claims it is false as evidence of collusion.

name: Gruagachan
description: A loose association of Pictish wizards (singular gruagach) who use the Pictish language in their magic and focus on affecting themselves and individuals; accepted into House Ex Miscellanea despite being unable to learn parma magica.

name: Praeses Septentrionalis
description: The Northern Guard, a group of covenants formed by Pralix to watch for Damhan-allaidh's return; destroyed in 889.

name: Clan Mac Gruagach
description: Highland clan of gruagachan that joined the Ordo in 816 and leads the Highland covenants of Loch Leglean.

name: Kelledei
description: The cele de ('servants of God'), communities of Scottish Church brothers who left monasteries ruled by greedy lay abbats; they have no formal rule.

name: Cistercian Order
description: Religious order for which David I founded Melrose Abbey in 1136.

name: Scottish Church
description: The Celtic Church of Scotland, independent of Rome, emphasizing Love; its sites generate a calming Divine aura that augments rather than hinders magic.

name: Roman Church
description: The Church under the bishop of Rome, which prevailed at the Synod of Whitby and gradually displaced the Scottish Church.

name: House of Canmore
description: The royal line of Malcolm Canmore and Margaret that ruled Scotland in the 12th and 13th centuries.

name: Mac Williams
description: Rebellious descendants of King Duncan who repeatedly rose against the Canmore kings until crushed in 1230.

name: Comyn family
description: Powerful Scottish family that squabbled with Alan Durward during Alexander III's minority.

name: Goulis family
description: Hereditary seneschals of Scotland who hold Monksend castle and are rumored to worship the Devil.

name: Clan Mac Donald
description: Highland clan used as an example; its chief is called 'the Mac Donald'.

name: Picts
description: The northern people called Caledonians and later Picti by the Romans; they called themselves Cruithni and were conquered by the Scots.

name: Broch-builders
description: The mysterious original people of Scotland who built brochs; possibly the Fomoreach.

name: Fomoreach
description: Seafaring people of Irish legend from the North and East, possibly the Broch-builders.

name: Scots
description: Irish tribe (Scotti) that settled in the southwest and conquered the Picts, giving their name to Scotland.

name: Gaidhealtachd
description: The Highlands of the Gaelic-speaking peoples.

name: Horsingas
description: Anti-Norman covenant of Saxon renegades in the South, founded 1070, the strongest military power in the Borders; raids English castles.

name: Crun Clach
description: Covenant founded in 954 that is the voice of the Lowland covenants, led by Caitlin Suil Uaine; the Pact of Crun Clach was made there.

name: Mac Gruagach
description: Covenant of Clan Mac Gruagach, one of the three dominant covenants of Loch Leglean, leading the Highland covenants.

name: Heart's Delight
description: Covenant of the Praeses Septentrionalis destroyed in one night by Damhan-allaidh in the late 880s.

name: Uamh na Croig
description: Covenant destroyed by giants in 977 after its magi hunted the giants for sport.

name: Holy Oak
description: Diedne covenant founded in 817 and destroyed during the Schism War.

name: The Well of the Head
description: Diedne covenant founded in 834 that sponsored Druids' Dale; destroyed in the Schism War.

name: Druids' Dale
description: Diedne covenant sponsored by the Well of the Head in 956; destroyed in the Schism War.

name: Peanhafel
description: Pictish covenant destroyed by Druids of House Diedne in a year-long siege in 849.

name: Blackthorn
description: Covenant mentioned in a Flambeau letter complaining that judgment had not been passed on it.

name: Durenmar
description: Place where the Order of Hermes was founded in 767.

name: Damhan-allaidh
description: Scottish wizard ('the Spider') who practiced blood and sacrifice magic, refused to join the Order, and fought Pralix; his body vanished after his defeat and he is thought to survive.

name: Pralix
description: Maga of House Tytalus (filia of Tytalus) who fought Damhan-allaidh with native magicians and founded the Ordo Miscellanea.

name: Ignes Festi
description: Flambeau magus who survived Loch Oadh with Pralix, quarreled with Brude Deathless, and died fighting Damhan-allaidh alone.

name: Brude Deathless
description: Mighty gruagach at least 400 years old whose soul is hidden; allied with Pralix and crippled invading Flambeau magi with Curses and Geasa in 1099.

name: Trianoma
description: Maga of House Bonisagus who helped form the Order and in 817 healed the breach with the Ordo Miscellanea.

name: Tytalus
description: Founder of House Tytalus, Pralix's parens.

name: Whitburh Frithowebba
description: The only quaesitor in Loch Leglean, of Horsingas; turns a blind eye to minor infractions of the Code.

name: Caitlin Suil Uaine
description: Canny diplomat of Crun Clach who leads the Lowland covenants.

name: Gwynasere
description: Venerable recipient of a Flambeau letter complaining about Horsingas.

name: William Fireheart
description: Flambeau magus who co-wrote a letter complaining about Horsingas.

name: Dan O'Thunder
description: Flambeau magus who co-wrote a letter complaining about Horsingas.

name: Thomas Verus
description: Redcap of House Mercere who migrated to Loch Leglean and wrote a letter describing it.

name: Mihalpi
description: Primus of House Mercere, addressee of Thomas Verus's letter.

name: Lord Goulis
description: Seneschal of the realm, rumored to be king of the Scottish diabolists.

name: Michael Scot
description: Wizard who subdued a demon in 1188 and had it sunder Eildon hill into three.

name: Queen of Elfland
description: Faerie ruler of the community in the Eildon Hills.

name: Thomas the Rhymer
description: Subject of a ballad about the road to fair Elfland.

name: Calgacus
description: Leader of the Caledonians killed at Mons Graupius in A.D. 84.

name: Sodric
description: Legendary king of the Picts from Scythia killed by Marius, per Geoffrey of Monmouth.

name: Marius
description: Legendary British king, son of Arvirarous, who killed Sodric and gave the Picts Caithness.

name: Geoffrey of Monmouth
description: Chronicler whose Historia Regum Britanniae (1136) is quoted about the Picts.

name: Cruithne
description: Ancestor of the Cruithni.

name: St. Ninian
description: Holy man trained by St. Martin of Tours who brought Christianity to the southern Picts and built Candida Casa in 397.

name: St. Martin of Tours
description: Saint who trained St. Ninian.

name: St. Columba
description: Irish monk who came to Iona in 565 and baptized the Pictish king Brude Mac Maelchon.

name: Brude Mac Maelchon
description: Northern Pictish king baptized by St. Columba.

name: St. Maelrubha
description: Saint associated with Applecross (601).

name: St. Oran
description: Saint of Dalriada who died in 548.

name: St. Mungo
description: Saint who built a church at Glasgow in 550.

name: St. Molaug
description: Saint of the Isle of Lismore (562).

name: St. Cuthbert
description: Saint of Lothian (580).

name: St. Aidan
description: Saint of Northumbria and Holy Isle (580).

name: Nechtan
description: King of the Picts who accepted the Roman Church in 710.

name: Brude son of Bile
description: Pictish king who consolidated North and South Picts 672-693.

name: Kenneth Mac Alpin
description: King of the Scots who stood on the Stone of Destiny in 834 and conquered the Picts with the aid of House Diedne.

name: Malcolm II
description: Scottish king who defeated the Angles at Carham in 1018.

name: Duncan I
description: Grandson of Malcolm II who became King of Scots in 1034; killed by MacBeth.

name: MacBeth
description: Mormaer of Moray who killed Duncan with the aid of Pictish wizards and renegade Ex Miscellanea magi, ruled seventeen years, and was killed by Malcolm Canmore.

name: Lulach
description: MacBeth's stepson, last truly Scottish High King, slain after eight months.

name: Malcolm III Canmore
description: Duncan's son raised in England who killed MacBeth with the aid of two mysterious magi and brought English influence to Scotland.

name: Siward of Northumbria
description: Duncan's brother-in-law who aided Malcolm Canmore.

name: Queen Margaret
description: English princess, wife of Malcolm Canmore, who brought the Roman Church to Scotland; canonized in 1230.

name: Edgar Atheling
description: Margaret's brother and heir to the Saxon crown of England.

name: Donald Ban
description: Malcolm Canmore's brother who resisted English influence and was twice king before being blinded by Edgar.

name: Duncan II
description: Malcolm's son raised in the Norman court, made king by William Rufus, then murdered.

name: Edgar
description: Malcolm's son who seized the throne from Donald Ban and founded Edinburgh Castle.

name: Bethoc
description: Daughter and heir of Donald Ban torn apart by her own hunting dogs.

name: Alexander I
description: King of Scotland 1107-1124.

name: David I
description: King of Scotland from 1124 who molded the kingdom on the Anglo-Norman model, founded royal burghs and Melrose Abbey.

name: Malcolm IV
description: King called 'the Maiden' for his vow of celibacy; traded David's southern gains for Huntington.

name: William the Lion
description: King of Scotland 1165-1214 who strengthened feudalism and bought back independence with the Quit-Claim of Canterbury.

name: Alexander II
description: King of Scotland from 1214, aged twenty-two in 1220, who signed the Magna Carta.

name: Alexander III
description: King of Scotland 1249-1286 whose death without heirs led to the succession crisis.

name: Margaret, Maid of Norway
description: Granddaughter and heir of Alexander III, who died crossing from Norway in 1290.

name: Robert Bruce
description: Claimant to the Scottish throne named successor by Alexander II.

name: Robert the Bruce
description: Grandson of the claimant Robert Bruce who leads armies against the English after 1298.

name: John Balliol
description: Claimant chosen king by Edward I in 1292 and later deposed.

name: John Comyn
description: Leader who rivals Robert the Bruce and attacks him in Selkirk forest in 1299.

name: William Wallace
description: Scottish rebel who wins at Stirling Bridge in 1297 and is defeated at Falkirk in 1298.

name: Edward I of England
description: English king who arbitrates the Scottish succession and conquers Scotland.

name: Hugh de Cressingham
description: Hated Treasurer of Scotland flayed after Stirling Bridge.

name: John de Warrenne
description: Earl of Surrey and Governor of Scotland who advances against Wallace.

name: Alan Durward
description: Justiciar who squabbled with the Comyns.

name: Earl Harald
description: Earl of Orkney (Harald Maddaderson) who invaded Moray and Ross from 1197; his family was cursed to be bellicose.

name: Thorfinn son of Harald
description: Son of Earl Harald blinded and castrated by William the Lion.

name: Guthred
description: Great-grandson of Duncan invited by the Mac Williams in 1211; captured and beheaded.

name: Magnus Barelegs
description: King of Norway who acquired the Western Isles in 1098 by dragging a ship across Kintyre.

name: Harald Hardrada
description: King of Norway killed at Stamford Bridge in 1066.

name: Harold Godwinson
description: English king killed at Hastings.

name: William the Conqueror
description: Duke of Normandy who conquered England and forced Malcolm to recognize him as overlord.

name: William Rufus
description: King of England who sent Duncan II to take the Scottish throne.

name: Edward the Confessor
description: English king at whose court Malcolm Canmore grew up.

name: Henry II of England
description: Henry Plantagenet, English king who captured William the Lion.

name: Richard the Lionheart
description: English king who sold William the Lion back his independence in 1189.

name: King John of England
description: English king who knighted Alexander II.

name: Henry III of England
description: English king ambivalent toward Scotland.

name: King Haakon
description: Norwegian king whose invasion failed at Largs in 1263.

name: Archbishop Thurstan
description: Archbishop of York who defeated David at the Battle of the Standard.

name: Guillame de Bruyse
description: Bishop of St. Andrews and primate of the Church in Scotland.

name: Somerled
description: Leader of rebellions in Argyll and the Islands 1140-1164.

name: Godred Crovan
description: King of Man and the Isles 1079-1095.

name: Harald Fairhair
description: Norwegian king who created the earldom of the Orkneys.

name: Rognvald Kolsson
description: Earl of Orkney who crusaded in 1152 and was canonized in 1192; a poet boasting of nine skills.

name: Sigurd the Stout
description: Earl of Orkney who died at Clontarf.

name: Thorfinn the Mighty
description: Earl of Orkney 1045-1065.

name: Finn Mac Coul
description: Gaelic hero of Highland stories.

name: Ossian
description: Gaelic hero of Highland stories.

name: CuChulainn
description: Gaelic hero of Highland stories.

name: Satan
description: Seen by Highlanders as a figure of ridicule.

name: Hagbui
description: An undead Viking barrow-dweller that guards buried treasure, with powers such as Rock Swimming, Reanimation and Immunity to Edged Weapons; Magic Might 10.

name: Giants
description: Highland giants over thirty feet tall who allied with Damhan-allaidh; magi were warned to leave them alone after Uamh na Croig.

name: Sluagh
description: The undead spirits of the Highlands that Damhan-allaidh unleashed on Loch Leglean in 815.

name: Trow
description: Solitary faeries of the Northern Islands, possibly related to trolls, one- or two-headed and restricted in sunlight.

name: Stoorworm
description: A poisonous water serpent as long as a ship with poison breath; Magic Might 42.

name: Cirein Croin
description: Ancestor of all stoorworms, so large it circled Britain; its teeth became the Northern Islands and its body Iceland.

name: Well worms
description: Serpents of northern England and southern Scotland related to the stoorworm.

name: Merrows
description: Supernatural aquatic creatures to be avoided when fishing.

name: Sith
description: Scots Gaelic term for faeries (Irish 'sidhe'), which sometimes inflame clan feuds.

name: Seelie faeries
description: Bands of benign faeries of the Lowlands who appreciate talented musicians.

name: Faeries
description: The dominant supernatural beings of the Scottish landscape; the good folk, called elves on the Borders.

name: Demons
description: Beings of Hell, hitherto unknown in Scotland until they came north with the Normans.

name: Scotland
description: Mythic Scotland, the land covered by the Loch Leglean Tribunal, divided into Highlands, Lowlands, Borders and Islands.

name: Highlands
description: The northern mountainous part of Scotland ruled by clans and home to solitary faeries.

name: Lowlands
description: Southern and eastern Scotland ruled by Norman-Scottish nobles in the English manner.

name: Borders
description: Border region between England and Scotland, lawless and raided by families on both sides.

name: Islands
description: The Scottish islands, Norse in culture.

name: Hadrian's Wall
description: Roman wall between the Solway and Tyne, the southern border of the Loch Leglean Tribunal.

name: Antonine Wall
description: Roman wall between the Forth and Clyde.

name: Caledonian Forest
description: Primeval hardwood forest covering much of the Highlands.

name: Loch Oadh
description: Loch where Damhan-allaidh ambushed Pralix in 814.

name: Loch Ochy
description: Site of Pralix's battle with Damhan-allaidh in 815.

name: Loch Leglean (place)
description: Pralix's winter camp and hidden town where tribunal meetings occur every seven years.

name: Cad Gadu
description: Forest on the Welsh border where Damhan-allaidh hid and Pralix had her base.

name: Carnac
description: Site in Brittany where Damhan-allaidh defeated Hermetic magi in 808.

name: Brittany
description: Where Damhan-allaidh lived in the late 8th century.

name: Caithness
description: Northern province settled by Norsemen; site of a battle with Damhan-allaidh.

name: Orkney Islands
description: Northern islands owned by Norway, rich in standing stones; once called the Orcades, Isles of the Dead.

name: Shetland Islands
description: Northern islands owned by Norway, where domestic animals are enchanted to half size.

name: Nordreys
description: The Northern Islands, Orkney and Shetland collectively.

name: Mainland
description: Name of the largest island in both Orkney and Shetland.

name: Ring of Brodgar
description: Stone circle on Mainland in Orkney that leads to the faerie realm of Barathrum.

name: Hebrides
description: Western islands held by the king of Norway until 1266.

name: Isle of Man
description: Vis-rich island claimed by three tribunals.

name: Iona
description: Small western island granted to St. Columba; raided by Vikings in 795.

name: Candida Casa
description: St. Ninian's whitewashed church at Whithorn.

name: Applecross
description: Site of the Monastery of St. Maelrubha, granted the earldom of Ross.

name: Stone of Destiny
description: Ancient relic that cries out when the rightful king stands on it; taken by Edward I.

name: Dunadd
description: Former capital of the Scottish kingdom.

name: Scone
description: Where Scottish kings are enthroned.

name: Northumbria
description: Anglian kingdom in northern Britain.

name: Strathclyde
description: British kingdom inherited by Duncan.

name: Moray
description: Northern region ruled by MacBeth and Lulach's descendants.

name: Eildon Hills
description: Hollow hills near Melrose containing a faerie community led by the Queen of Elfland, with regio leading to Arcadia; split into three by Michael Scot's demon.

name: Melrose Abbey
description: Cistercian abbey founded in 1136, plundered by Horsingas.

name: Monksend Castle
description: Castle of the Goulis family, originally a monastery.

name: Edinburgh
description: Capital of Scotland, a royal burgh with about 1,500 inhabitants.

name: Holyrood
description: Abbey at the end of Edinburgh's Royal Mile.

name: Berwick
description: Royal burgh and mint.

name: Roxburgh
description: Site of a royal mint.

name: Carlisle
description: Border seaport near Hadrian's Wall.

name: Bamburgh
description: Border town and royal burgh.

name: Cheviot Hills
description: Lawless hills where Horsingas raids freely.

name: St. Andrews
description: Seat of the primate of the Scottish Church.

name: Ben Nevis
description: Tallest mountain in Scotland.

name: Strathnavar
description: Highland area reached by the invading Flambeau in 1099.

name: Kintyre
description: Peninsula claimed by Magnus Barelegs.

name: Selkirk
description: Site of an English victory over the Scots and Selkirk forest.

name: Stirling
description: Site of Wallace's victory at Stirling Bridge.

name: Falkirk
description: Where Wallace was defeated in 1298.

name: Alnwick
description: Where Malcolm Canmore was killed.

name: Largs
description: Site of the battle of 1263.

name: Dalriada
description: Scottish kingdom in Argyll.

name: Lismore
description: See created in 1190, and Isle of Lismore.

name: Dunkeld
description: See and royal burgh.

name: Glasgow
description: Cathedral city where St. Mungo built a church.

name: Aberdeen
description: Royal burgh and see.

name: Brechin
description: Royal burgh and see.

name: Forfar
description: Where the last Mac William was killed.

name: Mons Graupius
description: Battle of A.D. 84 where Romans defeated the Caledonians.

name: Comraich
description: The sanctuary lands of a Scottish Church monastery, protected by its Dominion.

name: Knowe
description: Hollow hill abode of faeries.

name: Broch
description: Large thick-walled stone towers built by the Broch-builders.

name: Royal Burghs
description: Towns granted special privileges by the crown, with tollbooth and market cross.

name: Somniare
description: Part of Arcadia reached through the Eildon Hills.

name: Arcadia
description: The realm of the faeries, divided into six known lands.

name: Sorinbrus
description: One of the six known lands of Arcadia: the land of dreams.

name: Atlantium
description: One of the six known lands of Arcadia: the land under the sea.

name: Antrum
description: One of the six known lands of Arcadia: the land under the ground.

name: Wyrd
description: One of the six known lands of Arcadia: the land of the air.

name: Barathrum
description: One of the six known lands of Arcadia: the land of the dead, reached via the Ring of Brodgar.

name: Tartarus
description: One of the six known lands of Arcadia: the land of the beyond.

name: Dominion
description: The Divine realm; the Scottish Church's Dominion has a special calming effect.

name: Scottish Dominion
description: The Divine aura of Scottish Church sites, focused on the founder's bell and staff; it dampens Passions and Personality Traits and lets acclimated magi cast as if in a magic aura.

name: Hell
description: Infernal realm whose minions have shown little interest in the Highlands.

name: Parma Magica
description: Hermetic protective magic that gruagachan cannot learn.

name: Code of Hermes
description: The law of the Order, including the prohibition on interfering with mundane society.

name: Tribunal
description: Hermetic regional meeting held every seven years at Loch Leglean.

name: Aonaran
description: An independent magus owing allegiance to no covenant; a quarter of Loch Leglean magi.

name: Pact of Crun Clach
description: Pact of 1189 in which Scottish magi swore not to aid kings or invaders, regulating raids and theft.

name: Schism War
description: War of 1003-1012 in which House Diedne was destroyed.

name: Wizards' War
description: Hermetic formal conflict threatened by Clan Mac Gruagach.

name: Vis
description: Magical raw material; covenants raid each other's vis sources.

name: Magic Might
description: Measure of a creature's magical power.

name: Aura
description: Supernatural influence of a place.

name: Regio
description: Layered supernatural levels, as inside the Eildon Hills.

name: Age of Aries
description: Hermetic reckoning of time beginning 139 B.C.

name: Sigil
description: Voting token given to other magi at tribunal.

name: External Soul
description: Highland magicians' ability to remove their soul and hide it in an object, becoming unable to die while it is undisturbed.

name: Battle of the Great Light
description: Final battle in 816 where a false sun lit the sky and Pralix defeated Damhan-allaidh.

name: Night of the Sluagh
description: Attack of the sluagh on Loch Leglean in December 815.

name: Battle of the Bloody Glen
description: Battle of August 815 where Damhan-allaidh was wounded.

name: Synod of Whitby
description: 664 council declaring only the Roman Church should hold sway in the British Isles.

name: Quit-Claim of Canterbury
description: Document by which Richard I sold William the Lion back Scotland's independence.

name: Magna Carta
description: Charter signed by Alexander II at Runnymede.

name: Treaty of Perth
description: 1266 treaty recognizing Man and the Western Isles as Scottish.

name: Battle of the Standard
description: 1138 battle where Archbishop Thurstan defeated David.

name: Ceann cath
description: The chief of a Highland clan.

name: Seanachaidh
description: Clan storyteller and historian.

name: Tanaiste
description: The appointed successor of a clan chief.

name: Ollamh
description: Trained storyteller of chiefs and lairds.

name: Caterans
description: Landless men adopted into a clan.

name: Mormaer
description: Great steward; the seven mormaers became earls.

name: Abbat
description: The secular owner of a Scottish monastery.

name: Comarb
description: The religious leader of a Scottish monastery.

name: Ab
description: Founding leader and owner of a Scottish monastery.

name: Handfast
description: Highland trial marriage.

name: Ceilidh
description: Gathering to tell stories and sing.

name: Shinty
description: Highland stick-and-ball game enjoyed also by faeries.

name: Clach neart
description: Stone of strength used as a test of manhood.

name: Galloglaichs
description: Orcadian mercenaries fighting in chain mail with two-handed axes.

name: Hot-trod
description: Right to pursue a cattle thief across the border.

name: Odal law
description: Norwegian law granting a dead earl's lands to surviving sons.

name: Geasa
description: Supernatural prohibitions used by Brude Deathless to cripple magi.

name: Legio IX Hispana
description: Roman legion that marched north in 118 and vanished; ghost sightings are reported.

name: Cult of Mithra
description: Roman army cult with temples along the walls lacking magical power.

name: Cult of Mercury
description: Roman magical cult not a major factor along the walls.

name: Second Sight
description: Extraordinary Talent of prophecy common in Scottish history.

name: Curse
description: Extraordinary Talent used by hagbui and Brude Deathless.

name: Geas
description: Extraordinary Talent that may be used by hagbui.

name: Shape Shifter
description: Extraordinary Talent that some hagbui use.

name: Brawl
description: Ability of the hagbui.

name: Track
description: Ability of the hagbui.

name: Corpus
description: Hermetic Art; vis of this Art is found in the hagbui.

name: Animal
description: Hermetic Art; vis of this Art is found in the stoorworm.

name: Perdo
description: Hermetic Art; vis of this Art is found in the stoorworm.

name: Rock Swimming
description: Hagbui power (MuCo 40) to swim through stone or earth.

name: Fall of Darkness
description: Hagbui power (PeIg 25) creating a circle of darkness.

name: Fearful Aura
description: Hagbui power (ReMe 20) panicking one opponent a round.

name: Wind Raising
description: Hagbui power (ReAu 20) raising gale-force winds.

name: Confuse
description: Hagbui power (ReMe 15) like Confusion of the Numbed Will.

name: Mist Raising
description: Hagbui power (CrAu 10) raising a corpse-smelling mist.

name: Dull Weapon
description: Hagbui power (PeTe 5) reducing a weapon's damage bonus to zero.

name: Reanimation
description: Permanent hagbui power (CrCo 45) healing a body level per round.

name: Immunity to Edged Weapons
description: Permanent hagbui power (MuCo 35).

name: Stink
description: Hagbui power (CrAu 10) like Stench of the Twenty Corpses.

name: Confusion of the Numbed Will
